missions.title: A metered pod month: every (fake) dollar a mind spends is charged by the system to that mind, and its self-report no longer counts
missions.question: Can the Runtime wake a spending mind only when the system meters it, and can every dollar of a run be attributed to one agent from the meter alone? (Era I EC4; vision M4)
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-001.py → a two-mind pod (PM + Analyst) on the fake metered provider lives a month under an injected numeric cap on a local App; prints, per agent, the provisioner's charges, the App's system-reported cost and the self-report gap (equal / non-zero), the leaderboard costs taken from the meter, the sum of metered $ == the provisioner's total, and that the same specs under the real law (cap null) are refused before physics is told
missions.notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-6b (ADR-041 §8): gate lets a `metered` provider wake under a numeric cap; provision mints one key per agent (limit ≤ MAX_METERED_USD_MICROS, total ≤ cap); FakeMeteredProvider charges the FakeProvisioner; sync after the last step; fail loudly on a 422 label; expose reader conflicts/malformed (c34 WARN 3); Reuse runtime/metering.py (FakeProvisioner, sync_costs), runtime/gate.py decide_wake_under(provider, adapter, law), app metering endpoint. The real governance cap stays null: a numeric cap exists only as an injected Governance in tests/acceptance; the CLI never accepts an injected law (Art. 4). IDEAS c34: one whole-ledger invariant (sum of authoritative costs == sum of per-key maxima) is the EC4 assertion. RED-TEAM: yes (gate + metering). Parked, not in scope: B-000k (pod-less firm spend), B-000n (cost-report rate), B-022 (secret scan — before any real key). Deferred by the plan (cycle 38): (1) the compare-ledgers law for a metered recording; M-001 refuses `--cassette` on a metered run, so no metered run can be replayed yet. (2) The O(n²) scan in `record_metered_usage` does not matter at one sync per run; it stays in BACKLOG.

missions.title: A run is a self-contained proof object: one cassette file is enough to re-live a month and prove its ledger identical
missions.question: Can anyone re-run a recorded month from the cassette alone (no flags to remember) and get a machine verdict 'identical ledger' or the first divergence? (Era I EC2 path, ticked only with real minds; vision §1 proof objects; prerequisite of the fork instrument)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime backtest --specs specs/desk-month --steps 31 --cassette $TMPDIR/m.cassette.json, then uv run fund-runtime replay --cassette $TMPDIR/m.cassette.json --verify → 'IDENTICAL: <n> events, 0 differences, $0' (and a tampered cassette → 'DIVERGED at <wake/step>')
missions.notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-4b-2b: cassette v2 carries run parameters (steps, days_per_step, max_tool_calls, workflow_input), each spec's digest, each wake's model, optional tools_sha256; reader size cap; c32 NOTE 4 (a replay setup error must not read as diverged:…:ended); c32 NOTE 5 (`key` can mislabel a surface change); replay into a fresh DB and run app/ledger/compare.py in one command; a cassette step in scripts/smoke_run.py. v1 cassettes must still be read (or refused by name, decided by ADR). Reuse runtime/cassette.py, runtime/replay.py, runtime/cli.py, app/ledger/compare.py (read-only, one allowed difference — never widen it). Fold B-051 (operator read `fund-env run-minds`, smoke uses it) if it costs < 1/2 session. RED-TEAM: no unless the plan touches the gate or physics; the auditor checks the claim 'one file is enough'. If cassette v2 carries a metered run (M-001), this mission owns the trailing `cost_metered` block law in `app/ledger/compare.py`, by its own ADR (sketch in ADR-044 §6). Otherwise the first mission that replays a metered run (R-8) owns it.

missions.title: The desk pod exists as real OpenClaw agents in an isolated firm profile, certified by `fund-runtime openclaw doctor` (100% static checks); an uncertified mind never wakes
missions.question: Can the firm's minds be set up to the 08_OPENCLAW.md standard by code alone — generated, isolated from the Human's agents, deny-by-default — and refused a wake when they are not? (Era I EC7 static half; deliverable 6b; vision M5)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime openclaw render --specs specs/desk-month && uv run fund-runtime openclaw doctor → one line per firm- agent, static checks 1–5 PASS, live probes 6–10 SKIPPED (cap null); then a hand-edited workspace file → doctor FAIL (hash drift) and the Runtime refuses to wake that mind
missions.notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-7 (B-012, B-012a, B-012b, B-023s seal keys, B-000l loopback MCP URL); OCT POC charters → AgentSpec templates (08 §6). Rule zero first: verify every command and file name against the installed version (/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw), pin it in runtime/openclaw/VERSION_NOTES.md. Rule one: never touch the Human's ~/.openclaw or any non-firm- agent; backup under umask 077 before the first change. The Builder's Bash sandbox can write only the repo and $TMPDIR: the architect must first verify whether the installed OpenClaw can keep a profile's state/config under a directory we choose (env or flag). If yes, the acceptance check renders + applies + doctors inside a temp dir. If no, split by capability: (a) render + every static check that reads only rendered artifacts, run in a temp dir; (b) apply to ~/.openclaw-firm as a step the Human runs once (question in state/QUESTIONS.md). The acceptance check must skip nothing silently: if `openclaw` is absent it FAILS (it is installed here). Gate change 'no conformance → no wake' → RED-TEAM: yes. Live probes stay skipped while the cap is null (Q-0001).

missions.title: Physics refuses instead of crashing, and a run it will refuse leaves no trace: the 9 open strict xfails pass
missions.question: Are the known physics holes closed before minds that register, message and trade at small size arrive (before vision M6 / R-8)?
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-004.py → lists each of the 9 hole tests (red-team 0001 ×3, 0004 ×1, 0009 ×2, 0020 ×3) and PASS for each, with xfail markers removed; plus a live App: register into a missing pod → 404/409, not 500
missions.notes: Bundle: B-056 (+B-019, same root: register with a missing/absent pod → 500; fix in app.registry.service.register_agent), B-055 ×2 (_conduct reads /agents + pods + published tool list before declare_minds), B-000g ×2 (byte caps on structured_payload and task outcome), B-000e (message body + structured_payload on message_sent), B-026 (fee under $5 notional pays $0.00 — a fee-law change: ADR), B-036 ×2 (OMS_LOCK per process; cross-process advance vs fill). B-036 may be larger than the rest: the architect may cut it to its own later mission or accept it by ADR with its reason (Art. 9: a hole accepted is written, never hidden). Acceptance runs the named tests with the markers gone (it fails today because they xfail). New red-team lows found during M-001..M-003 land here. RED-TEAM: yes. From M-001's red-team (tests/test_redteam_0021.py, 3 strict xfails; ADR-044): (medium) mid-run leaderboard ranks metered minds on self-report until the one sync - fix = post every key at 0 after provision, which needs the trailing-block compare-ledgers law written with it; (medium) inbox-stuffing drains a metered mind's key - per-sender message quota (law change, ADR); (low) a part-way sync failure reports posted 0 and counts every key unattributed. Also (auditor, c38): now that the Human set a cap and left a provisioning key (Q-0001/2 answered 2026-10-15), ADR-044 §4 'monthly accounting across runs before any real key' must become a check in code before any real provider name joins METERED_PROVIDERS - with B-022 (secret scan).

missions.title: A Truman shock: a scenario file crashes a market on day d of a keyed synthetic month, `system` announces it, a pod lives through it, and the same key + scenario replays to the same ledger
missions.question: Can the world script events — the lever by which the Builder changes the world without touching a mind (Art. 10) — deterministically and on the record? (Era I deliverables 4–5: Truman v1 + world events; prerequisite of Era II EC2)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime backtest --specs specs/desk-month --steps 31 --scenario scenarios/crash-day-12.yaml → day 12: a `world_event` + `system` announcement in the ledger, the shocked ticker's close drops by the scenario's amount, the scripted pod's equity curve shows it; run twice → compare-ledgers IDENTICAL
serves: Era I deliverable 4 (Truman v1, synthetic half)
missions.notes: Raw material: B-007 (world events table + system announcements), B-008 (Truman v1). Built on the keyed synthetic market (ADR-030), not on a real-history pack: fetching real history needs network the Builder's sandbox does not have (the real-history pack is a later mission or a one-time command the Human runs). The scenario is part of the run's world (ADR-031: run_started.world records it; agents see 'withheld' per ADR-034, the announcement is what they are told). The look-ahead guard holds: no agent learns of a shock before its day. Whether an agent is told its data is synthetic is an experimental variable (08 §4) — record it per run. RED-TEAM: yes (marketdata).

missions.title: Central risk acts by law: a pod driven down by a Truman crash has its capital cut at 5% drawdown, goes reduce-only at 7.5% and is liquidated and closed at 10% — exactly, on the record
missions.question: Can physics enforce the firm's risk ladder (04_FIRM §5) deterministically, so a pod's death is a law, not a judgement? (Era II EC2: 'a forced-drawdown Truman scenario triggers 5% / 7.5% / 10% actions exactly')
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-006.py → a scripted pod lives a month with a 3-step crash scenario; prints the high-water mark, each threshold crossing (day, drawdown %), the ledger event for each action, a refused new-risk order after 7.5% (403/409 + event), and the pod closed with zero positions after 10%
missions.notes: Starts Era II while Era I's real-mind criteria wait on the Human's cap (ADR-043). 04_FIRM §5: drawdown from the pod's high-water mark within the generation; 5% → allocation cut to 50%, positions above the new limit reduced within 2 sim-days or by the OMS; 7.5% → reduce-only (+ mandatory review workflow: record the event only, the CRO/CEO workflow is a later mission); 10% → liquidated, closed for the generation. Firm-level 8%/12% and exposure limits: out of scope (next mission). Reuse app/metrics/equity.py and the OMS; every action is an event, derived state rebuildable from the ledger. RED-TEAM: yes (oms).
